introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2020. Duration: Two and a Half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Questions ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

(Sections: A Map Work, B Physical Geography, C Human Geography, D Cameroon Geography. Question 1 is the only question of Section A.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Identify the industry in **column one** and match it with the pull factors in **column two** that attract it.

| Column One | Column Two |
|---|---|
| (i) Manufacturing of electronics | A) Large market and transport |
| (ii) Iron and steel industry | B) Large number of work force and market |
| (iii) Baking of bread | C) Large source of raw material and power supply |
| (iv) Textile industry | D) Large number of highly skilled labour, power and market |

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Industry | Pull factor | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| (i) Manufacturing of electronics | **D** | It needs highly skilled workers and a lot of power, and it sells to a large market. |
| (ii) Iron and steel industry | **C** | It uses heavy raw materials (iron ore, coal or limestone) and a great deal of power, so it locates near them. |
| (iii) Baking of bread | **A** | Bread is perishable and bulky, so bakeries locate near the market and need good transport to deliver it fresh. |
| (iv) Textile industry | **B** | It uses many workers, and a large market buys its products. |

**Answer: (i) D, (ii) C, (iii) A, (iv) B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Describe **FOUR** strategies used by governments of NICs in developing their industries.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **newly industrialised countries (NICs)**, such as South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Hong Kong, Brazil and Mexico, used the following strategies:

1. **Export-oriented industrialisation:** the governments encouraged the manufacture of goods (electronics, textiles, ships, cars) for sale abroad, which earned foreign currency.
2. **Attracting foreign investment:** they offered tax holidays, cheap land and free-trade or export-processing zones to foreign companies, which brought capital and technology.
3. **Investing in education and training:** governments built schools and technical colleges to provide a skilled and disciplined labour force at low wages.
4. **Providing infrastructure and protecting young industries:** ports, roads, electricity and telecommunications were built, and tariffs or quotas protected young industries from foreign competition in the early years. National development plans guided the effort.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) On the outline map of the world provided, **locate** and **name**: **Two areas of low population densities; TWO highly industrialised regions, a major shipping route.**

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_5_fig_1.png)

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Shade or mark each area on the outline map and write its name beside it; draw the shipping route as a line with the name of the route. Approximate positions are given with the latitude and longitude scale on the frame.

**Two areas of low population density (name two).**

- The **Sahara Desert** in North Africa (about 15 to 30 degrees N, between 15 degrees W and 30 degrees E): hot, dry and almost empty.
- The **Amazon Basin** in South America (about 0 to 10 degrees S, 50 to 70 degrees W): dense forest and hot, wet climate.
- Also accepted: northern Canada and Siberia (cold), the Australian interior (desert), Greenland and Antarctica.

**Two highly industrialised regions (name two).**

- **North-western Europe** (the Ruhr and Rhine area, the English Midlands, northern France).
- **North-eastern United States** and the Great Lakes area.
- Also accepted: **Japan** (Tokyo-Osaka belt) and the Moscow region of Russia.

**A major shipping route (name one).** The **North Atlantic route** between western Europe (for example Rotterdam and Liverpool) and the north-east coast of North America (New York); or the **Suez Canal route** from the Mediterranean through the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean; or the **Cape route** round southern Africa; or the **Panama Canal route** between the Atlantic and the Pacific.

Marking: 2 marks for each of the three requirements (location and name).
themes: major industrial regions and shipping routes

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) Describe the differences in the level of development between AICs, and LICs by using the following measurements: **birth rate, death rate, GNP per head, literacy rate, population growth rate and Life expectancy.**

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**AICs** are the advanced industrial countries (for example Japan, the United States, Germany) and **LICs** are the low-income (developing) countries (for example Niger, Chad and many others in Africa). The differences are generally as follows.

| Measurement | AICs | LICs |
|---|---|---|
| Birth rate | **Low** (generally below about 15 per 1000 people) | **High** (generally above about 30 per 1000) because of early marriage, lack of family planning and the need for labour |
| Death rate | **Low** (about 8 to 12 per 1000), because of good medical care, nutrition and sanitation | **Higher** in the poorest countries (often 10 to 20 per 1000) because of disease, poor medical care and malnutrition |
| GNP per head | **High** (more than about 12 000 US dollars per person) | **Low** (about 1 000 US dollars or less in the poorest) |
| Literacy rate | **Very high** (generally above 95 per cent) | **Lower** (often well below 70 per cent, especially among women) |
| Population growth rate | **Low** (below 1 per cent a year, and sometimes nil or negative) | **High** (generally 2 to 3 per cent a year or more) |
| Life expectancy | **High** (about 75 to 85 years) | **Low** (about 50 to 65 years) |

In short, AICs are richer, healthier and more educated, with slow population growth, while LICs have fast population growth, low incomes and low living standards. (The figures are orders of magnitude; they change with each year's data.)
